source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក (Techniques for Banana Cultivation), 2019, section I.2 (សារៈប្រយូជន៍ដំណាំចេក)
text:
Banana fruit is naturally rich in simple sugars (sucrose, fructose, and glucose), which is why ripe fruit tastes very sweet and can provide a quick source of energy — studies cited in the source note that a person can obtain roughly 90 calories from one banana. Because banana contains no gluten, it is often recommended as a safe fruit for people with gluten sensitivity.

Banana also contains the amino acid tryptophan, which the body can convert into serotonin, a compound associated with improved mood and reduced stress; combined with vitamin B6, this makes banana a food that nutrition guidance often points to for supporting calm and emotional well-being. Banana is also a source of B-vitamins (B6, B12) and potassium, nutrients important for maintaining healthy nerve and muscle function, including for people recovering from illness.

Banana is naturally low in fat and contains no cholesterol, and it provides dietary fiber that supports digestion. This fiber content is also why banana is commonly given to infants and young children as an easily digestible early food, and why it is recommended for people with digestive difficulties. Nutrition education materials cited in the source note that up to 40% of the vitamin and mineral content found in ripe banana can be attributed to its balanced natural sugar and fiber profile, which is one reason banana is emphasized as a beneficial food for children's growth and for students needing sustained mental energy for study.
